items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember in New York Clare Fischer had flown out from L.A. He did these arrangements.

ctx.x: Then, Hubert, here we come to, again, another one of those benchmark recordings, In the Beginning. I’m just going to put a little footnote on this with Ken here. One of the things, when I was giving him lessons, was I made a recording of Airegin, Steve Gadd, the duet. So this is another one of those ones. So if you would like to talk about – Come Ye Disconsolate is on there.

Yeah, I can talk about that. I remember in New York Clare Fischer had flown out from L.A. He did these arrangements. As a matter of fact, I just heard it for the first time in years just last week, the first time, because someone sent me a download. I got it downloaded into my iPod.

That arrangement on In the Beginning is very special, to the point I would like to include it in my band, my band’s repertoire, because I haven’t played it since we did the recording. Never played it live.
